name: Sculpfun S30 Ultra 20W
tagline: Mid-tier S30 Ultra: strong diode cutting without CO₂ pricing
tldr: The 20W S30 Ultra is the balanced pick in the line: compressed beam cutting on thin wood, large community settings library, and the same stiff frame as the 22W refresh.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood in ~4–7 min in our benchmarks
Fills at ~67–134 mm/s: a 10 × 10 cm photo in ~7–12 min
Handles dark acrylic up to about 5 mm
cons: Naming is unclear on many listings: confirm the head model and optical power
More charring than the entry head on thin wood: air assist becomes necessary
Wider ~0.08 mm spot, so the finest photo detail is a little softer than on the entry head
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Sculpfun S30 Ultra. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

editorialDepth.advantages: Sculpfun S30 Ultra 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame: glasses and exhaust required. Upgrade path to 22W if cutting takes over. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

faq.question: Does Sculpfun actually sell an S30 Ultra 20W?
faq.answer: Sculpfun's own store lists the S30 Ultra with 11W, 22W and 33W heads. A listing sold as an S30 Ultra 20W is usually a reseller label for one of these heads, or a mix-up with the separate S30 Pro Max 20W. Check the head model and the optical power on the listing before paying.

faq.question: What does this configuration cut?
faq.answer: In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 4–7 min at 5–11 mm/s. Basswood up to about 8 mm is realistic in several passes with air assist, and dark acrylic up to about 5 mm. Clear acrylic stays out of reach, as on any diode.

faq.question: This configuration or the 22W S30 Ultra?
faq.answer: Our benchmarks for both are close: the same 4–7 min for a 3 mm square, with the 22W reaching slightly higher cut speeds (up to ~14 mm/s against ~11 mm/s). On our tracked listings this one runs $450–650 against $690 for the 22W LightBurn bundle, so pick whichever genuine SKU is cheaper once the air pump is included.

standoutFeatures.title: Cutting-ready speed
standoutFeatures.body: 3 mm basswood squares in about 4–7 min in our benchmarks, roughly twice as fast as the entry head.

standoutFeatures.title: Dark acrylic up to ~5 mm
standoutFeatures.body: Enough power for coloured and black acrylic signs and inlays, which the entry head struggles with.

standoutFeatures.title: Shared S30 Ultra frame
standoutFeatures.body: Same frame, adapter and cable as the other S30 Ultra heads, so parts and accessories are interchangeable.
